Bill.BriefDescription: Protecting the water quality in Hood Canal.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to protecting Hood Canal by removing nitrates andphosphates from onsite sewage disposal systems and wastewatertreatment plants; amending RCW 70.118B.040; adding a new section tochapter 90.88 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 70.118 RCW; addinga new section to chapter 70.118A RCW; and adding a new section tochapter 90.48 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.88 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In aquatic rehabilitation zone one, any new or retrofitted onsitesewage disposal systems or wastewater treatment systems installed afterJuly 1, 2009, must remove nitrates and phosphates to a level that at aminimum meets the department of ecology's water quality standards anddoes not adversely impact the health of Hood Canal.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.118 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW 90.88.010,any new or retrofitted onsite sewage disposal system installed after p. 1 HB 3227July 1, 2009, must remove nitrates and phosphates to a level that at aminimum meets the department of ecology's water quality standards anddoes not adversely impact the health of Hood Canal.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.118ARCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW 90.88.010,any new or retrofitted onsite sewage disposal system installed afterJuly 1, 2009, must remove nitrates and phosphates to a level that at aminimum meets the department of ecology's water quality standards anddoes not adversely impact the health of Hood Canal.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 70.118B.040 and 2007 c 343 s 5 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) For the protection of human health and the environment, thesecretary shall adopt rules for the comprehensive regulation of largeonsite sewage systems, which includes, but is not limited to, thesiting, design, construction, installation, maintenance, repair, andpermitting of the systems. (2) In adopting the rules, the secretary shall, in consultationwith the department of ecology, require that large onsite sewagesystems comply with the applicable sections of chapter 90.48 RCWregarding control and prevention of pollution of waters of the state,including but not limited to: (a) Surface and groundwater standards established under RCW90.48.035; and (b) Those provisions requiring all known, available, and reasonablemethods of treatment. (3) In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW90.88.010, any new or retrofitted large onsite sewage disposal systeminstalled after July 1, 2009, must remove nitrates and phosphates to alevel that at a minimum meets the department of ecology's water qualitystandards and does not adversely impact the health of Hood Canal. (4) In adopting the rules, the secretary shall ensure thatrequirements for large onsite sewage systems are consistent with therequirements of any comprehensive plans or development regulationsadopted under chapter 36.70A RCW or any other applicable comprehensive HB 3227 p. 2 plan, land use plan, or development regulation adopted by a city, town,or county.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 90.48 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In aquatic rehabilitation zone one as designated in RCW 90.88.010,any new or retrofitted wastewater treatment system installed after July1, 2009, must remove nitrates and phosphates to a level that at aminimum meets the department's water quality standards and does notadversely impact the health of Hood Canal.
